  • Reference

    Fit a RuleFit Model via LightGBM

    rule_ensemble_lgb.Rd

    rule_ensemble_lgb() fits a model.

    rule_ensemble_lgb(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
rule_ensemble_lgb(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
rule_ensemble_lgb(
  x,
  y,
  ...,
  weights = NULL,
  trees = 50,
  mtry = 1,
  learn_rate = 0.01,
  tree_depth = 4,
  min_n = 5,
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'matrix'
rule_ensemble_lgb(
  x,
  y,
  ...,
  weights = NULL,
  trees = 50,
  mtry = 1,
  learn_rate = 0.01,
  tree_depth = 4,
  min_n = 5,
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'formula'
rule_ensemble_lgb(
  formula,
  data,
  ...,
  weights = NULL,
  trees = 50,
  mtry = 1,
  learn_rate = 0.01,
  tree_depth = 4,
  min_n = 5,
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

# S3 method for class 'recipe'
rule_ensemble_lgb(
  x,
  data,
  ...,
  trees = 50,
  mtry = 1,
  learn_rate = 0.01,
  tree_depth = 4,
  min_n = 5,
  penalty = 0.001,
  mixture = 1,
  verbose = FALSE
)

    Arguments

    x

    Depending on the context:

    • A data frame of predictors.

    • A matrix of predictors.

    • A recipe specifying a set of preprocessing steps created from recipes::recipe().

    ...

    Named options for the boosting model and the glmnet model:

    • Options for lightgbm go to the boosting model. These are lightgbm's parameters and their aliases, and the arguments of lightgbm::lgb.train(), lightgbm::lgb.Dataset(), and bonsai::train_lightgbm() (e.g., lambda_l2, bagging_fraction, or counts).

    Options that rule_ensemble_lgb() sets itself (e.g., num_iterations or learning_rate) are errors; use the main arguments (e.g., trees or learn_rate) instead. Use verbose instead of quiet. See the "Boosting and glmnet options" section for how options are routed.

    y

    When x is a data frame or matrix, y is the outcome specified as:

    • A data frame with 1 numeric column.

    • A matrix with 1 numeric column.

    • A numeric vector.

    weights

    An optional vector of non-negative case weights with one value per row of the training set. It can be a numeric vector or one created by hardhat::importance_weights() or hardhat::frequency_weights(). Not used by the recipe method; see the "Case weights" section.

    trees

    An integer for the number of trees contained in the ensemble.

    mtry

    The proportion of predictors randomly sampled at each split, on (0, 1].

    learn_rate

    A number for the rate at which the boosting algorithm adapts from iteration-to-iteration (specific engines only). This is sometimes referred to as the shrinkage parameter.

    tree_depth

    An integer for the maximum depth of the tree (i.e. number of splits) (specific engines only).

    min_n

    The minimum number of data points in a node needed to split it further (min_data_in_leaf in lightgbm).

    penalty

    A non-negative number representing the total amount of regularization (specific engines only).

    mixture

    A number between zero and one (inclusive) denoting the proportion of L1 regularization (i.e. lasso) in the model.

    • mixture = 1 specifies a pure lasso model,

    • mixture = 0 specifies a ridge regression model, and

    • 0 < mixture < 1 specifies an elastic net model, interpolating lasso and ridge.

    Available for specific engines only.

    verbose

    A single logical. If TRUE, the boosting library prints its training log, and rule_ensemble_ctb() warns when min_n is given and ignored.

    formula

    A formula specifying the outcome terms on the left-hand side, and the predictor terms on the right-hand side.

    data

    When a recipe or formula is used, data is specified as:

    • A data frame containing both the predictors and the outcome.

    Value

    A rule_ensemble_lgb object that inherits from "rule_ensemble". See rule_ensemble-object for its elements.

    Case weights

    Case weights are used to fit both the boosted trees that create the rules and the glmnet model that is fit to the rules. Rows with a weight of zero are not used to decide which rules are removed for having a single unique value or being linear combinations of other columns.

    For the data frame, matrix, and formula methods, pass the weights to weights. A case weights column cannot also be a predictor. For the recipe method, add the weights as a column of data that is created by hardhat::importance_weights() or hardhat::frequency_weights(); recipes::recipe() gives these columns the "case_weights" role, so they are not used as predictors.

    Boosting and glmnet options

    Named options for the boosting model and the glmnet model are given together as one set in .... Each option is sent to one of the two models by its name:

    • Options for the boosting library go to the boosting model. The valid names depend on the library; see the ... argument of rule_ensemble_xgb(), rule_ensemble_lgb(), or rule_ensemble_ctb().

    • Arguments of glmnet::glmnet() go to the glmnet model (e.g., standardize or penalty.factor). path_values, a numeric vector of penalty values for the glmnet path, also goes to the glmnet model; see parsnip::glmnet-details for how it is used.

    A name that is valid for both models goes to the boosting model. An unknown name is an error. Options that rbe sets itself are also errors; use the main arguments (e.g., trees or learn_rate) instead.
